title: Building World Models from Intrinsic Motivation
abstract: arXiv:2611.13113v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In the absence of extrinsic rewards or task supervision, human behavior is guided by intrinsic motivation---neural signals that drive curiosity, creativity, play, and other essential facets of intelligence. Intrinsic motivation plays an important developmental role in building robust world models that enable generalization and adaptation. Yet existing studies leave open how a broad range of intrinsic motivations interacts with world-model representation learning to support downstream control. This limits our understanding of which intrinsically collected experiences build reusable models. To address these gaps, we integrate 24 intrinsic objectives, including established methods and explicit variants spanning curiosity, entropy, and competency, into a common model-based reinforcement learning framework. translated_title: 从内在动机构建世界模型
translated_abstract: 在缺乏外在奖励或任务监督的情况下，人类行为由内在动机引导——即驱动好奇心、创造力、游戏以及其他智能核心要素的神经信号。内在动机在构建能够实现泛化与适应的稳健世界模型方面发挥着重要的发育作用。然而，现有研究尚未解答：多种多样的内在动机如何与世界模型表示学习相互作用以支持下游控制。这限制了我们对哪些由内在动机收集的经验能够构建可复用模型的理解。为填补这些空白，我们将24种内在目标（包括涵盖好奇心、熵与胜任力等方向的成熟方法及显式变体）整合到一个统一的基于模型的强化学习框架中。我们通过在运动控制、物体操作和开放式游戏等任务中的零样本、少样本和多任务控制，来评估它们所构建的世界模型……
tldr: 该论文将24种内在动机目标统一整合到一个基于模型的强化学习框架中，系统评估了它们所构建的世界模型在零样本、少样本和多任务控制下的表现。
en_tdlr: This paper integrates 24 intrinsic motivation objectives—spanning curiosity, entropy, and competency—into a unified model-based reinforcement learning framework and systematically evaluates the world models they build through zero-shot, few-shot, and multi-task control.
